answer.origin: Primary source: NVIDIA Corporation Form 8-K (SEC EDGAR) dated and filed August 17, 2026, with Item 1.01 and Item 2.03 disclosure and Item 7.01 furnishing of press release Exhibit 99.1 issued the same day. Stated event time and publication day are both August 17, 2026. The company's own filing is the origin; no independent access was used.
answer.note: NVIDIA's own SEC filing states that on August 17, 2026 it entered multiple residual value guaranties with SB Energy (Lessor) covering leases for about 4.25 GW of IT load at the Portsmouth Site in Pike County, Ohio, with OpenAI Group PBC's affiliate as tenant. The filing describes NVIDIA's guaranteed-payment obligation as capped cumulatively at $105 billion for the initial commitment, with an additional roughly 3.8 GW of credit support available at NVIDIA's sole discretion. Payments are triggered only by a tenant Trigger Event (OpenAI insolvency causing lease default, or OpenAI payment failure), are measured as the shortfall between a guaranteed minimum lease value and amounts recovered by relet or sale, and are conditioned on the Lessor meeting ready-for-service conditions expected beginning in 2028. NVIDIA can then assume, relet, sell, terminate, or defer remedies up to one year. Obligations end at the earliest of the 20th anniversary of lease commencement, lease termination by OpenAI, OpenAI reaching a satisfactory credit rating, or other customary events. OpenAI reimburses and indemnifies NVIDIA for amounts NVIDIA actually pays. The filing says NVIDIA has secured land, power and shell capacity at the site to host NVIDIA AI compute infrastructure and that OpenAI will deploy NVIDIA's DSX AI factory platform there. Conditional reading: this is a material contingent financial commitment by NVIDIA, sized at up to $105 billion for the initial 4.25 GW, that becomes a cash obligation only if OpenAI as tenant defaults and the shortfall is not recovered, and that is not expected to bite before 2028 ready-for-service. It supports a view that NVIDIA is backing data center capacity to drive demand for its own platform, with OpenAI as the economic counterparty bearing the lease obligation and reimbursing NVIDIA.
limitations: The full text of the Agreements is not in the supplied source; the filing says it will be filed as an exhibit to the Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 26, 2026, so guaranteed minimum lease values, lease economics, fee terms and specific trigger definitions are unknown.

The $105 billion figure is a cumulative cap on the initial commitment, not an estimate of expected payments; no expected payment amount, probability of Trigger Event, or NVIDIA-side accounting treatment (such as reserves or fair value) is disclosed.
The approximately 3.8 GW of additional credit support is optional at NVIDIA's sole discretion and no amount or commitment is stated for it, so it should not be counted as committed exposure.
The ready-for-service timing (expected beginning 2028) is a company expectation stated in forward-looking language; the filing does not confirm the schedule or the Lessor's progress.
OpenAI's credit standing, lease payment capacity and the terms of its underlying lease obligations are not disclosed; the source does not show OpenAI's current financial condition.

The source states NVIDIA has secured land, power and shell capacity and that OpenAI will deploy DSX on this capacity, but does not give dates, MW figures for power delivery, or a construction or financing plan for SB Energy's build-out.
No historical records or independent corroboration were supplied, so the scale and timing claims rest on NVIDIA's own filing and press release.
follow_up: Obtain the Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 26, 2026 and extract the filed Agreements to check the guaranteed minimum lease values, trigger definitions, cap mechanics and remedy costs.
Check subsequent NVIDIA 10-Q and 10-K filings for any recognized liability, guarantee disclosure, or change in the $105 billion cap or the 3.8 GW optional credit support.
Monitor SB Energy and public announcements for ready-for-service milestones at the Portsmouth Site against the 2028 expectation, and any change in lease commencement dates.

Monitor OpenAI public disclosures on the Portsmouth lease, its payment status and any credit rating change, since these drive whether NVIDIA's payment obligation can be triggered and when obligations terminate.
Check whether the 3.8 GW credit support is exercised in later NVIDIA filings or SB Energy announcements.
